detailed_rationale: Viyash Scientific Limited (the ticker's current name) is a Hyderabad-headquartered animal-health pharmaceutical company -- active pharmaceutical ingredients, finished-dose veterinary formulations (cattle and poultry), and analytical services -- with operations extending to the US, Spain and elsewhere, present across 100+ countries. Critically, this is a freshly merged entity: the company was Sequent Scientific Limited until it merged with Viyash Life Sciences (NCLT-approved in 2024) and was renamed Viyash Scientific Limited in January 2026. FY26 (year to Mar 2026) results show revenue of about Rs 3,420 crore and net income up 663.5% YoY to about Rs 177 crore (EPS roughly Rs 4.01-4.06, up about 657% YoY) -- an explicit turnaround, with source commentary confirming Q4 FY25 'marked a turnaround from a loss-making position in the same period last year.' In other words, the eye-catching profit growth is substantially a base-effect recovery from a loss-making pre-turnaround/pre-merger period, not a clean read of organic operating momentum. Reported revenue growth also varies meaningfully by source and period definition: the quant screen shows revenue_growth_1y of 58.6% (and a 3-year CAGR of 34.0%, hence its own growth_divergence_flag being True), while a separate FY26 annual read shows revenue growth of only about 13.8% YoY -- a real discrepancy most likely explained by how the Sequent-Viyash merger is being reflected across different trailing-period bases (pro-forma combined vs standalone-legacy comparisons), which is exactly the kind of merger/demerger base-effect distortion the analyst process is meant to catch rather than credit at face value. The quant screen's trailing ROE of -3.41% (which drives its very low quality_score of 7.9) likely reflects a trailing window that still captured loss-making pre-turnaround quarters; more current data shows ROE around 7.4% (last year) and only about 3.8% on a 3-year average basis -- weak in absolute terms, but positive and clearly on an improving trajectory, not the negative figure the quant screen currently shows. Working capital has deteriorated (71.6 to 111 days), a real efficiency concern to watch through the merger-integration period. The balance sheet is modestly levered (D/E about 0.17x, interest coverage about 9.5x) and debt has reportedly been reduced. The company does not pay a dividend, consistent with an entity still reinvesting through a major integration. A further international bolt-on is pending: a share purchase agreement to acquire 100% of BioForLife Italia for EUR 16.976 million, subject to Italian regulatory clearance, extending the animal-health formulation footprint into Europe. Management's own forward guidance following the FY26 results is for '15% annual growth and continued margin strength' -- a useful, company-supplied anchor for the true forward run-rate once the merger-related noise is set aside. At a PE in the high-50s (57.5x per the quant screen, 58.2x per more current data) against this backdrop, the stock is pricing a durable growth-and-margin story on top of what is genuinely a very recent, merger-driven earnings turnaround.
recommendation_rationale: The quant screen carries this as Hold: an extremely low quality_score (7.9, driven by the -3.41% trailing ROE) sits oddly alongside a very high growth_1y_score (94.2) and its own growth_divergence_flag is already True -- the screen itself is signaling that something about this stock's growth/quality read does not hang together cleanly, which my research confirms is the Sequent Scientific-to-Viyash Scientific merger (NCLT-approved 2024, renamed January 2026) distorting both the ROE base and the reported growth rate. I am not able to rescue a quant-Hold further nor override it to Sell, and the recommendation stays Hold, but this is a genuine methodology-relevant case: the quant quality_score of 7.9 is very likely an artifact of a merger-affected trailing ROE rather than a true read on this business's current profitability, which could be misleading if taken at face value elsewhere in the same batch (any other recently-merged or renamed entity could show the same distortion). I am escalating for that reason, not because I believe the call should be different today.
summary: Viyash Scientific (until January 2026, Sequent Scientific) is a veterinary/animal-health pharmaceutical company making active ingredients and finished formulations for cattle and poultry, recently combined with Viyash Life Sciences in a court-approved merger. The company has just turned around from a loss-making period into strong profit growth, and management is guiding to steady mid-teens growth with stable margins going forward, alongside a pending bolt-on acquisition in Italy. Because of the recent merger, however, the reported year-on-year growth and profitability figures are affected by how the combined entity compares to its pre-merger base, so they should be read with some caution rather than taken as a clean trend. We rate it a Hold: a real turnaround story in a consolidating global animal-health business, but one where the reported numbers need to be understood through the lens of the recent merger before being fully trusted.
positive_para: A genuine operating turnaround (net income up over 6x YoY in FY26, following an explicit prior-year loss-making comparison) in a growing global animal-health API and formulations business spanning 100+ countries, with management guiding to a steady 15% forward growth rate and continued margin strength, a pending European bolt-on acquisition (BioForLife Italia) extending the footprint, modest and reducing leverage, and a scale-consolidation rationale (the Sequent-Viyash merger) that could support real synergies over time.
negative_para: The eye-catching growth and profit-turnaround numbers are substantially a base-effect and merger-accounting artifact rather than a clean organic trend -- reported revenue growth varies from about 13.8% to 58.6% YoY depending on source/period basis, and the quant screen's own -3.41% trailing ROE (versus a more current, still-weak but positive 7.4%/3.8% range) reflects a loss-making window that has already passed. Working capital has deteriorated (71.6 to 111 days) through the merger-integration period, the company pays no dividend, and at a PE in the high-50s the market is pricing durability into a growth story whose recent numbers are not yet clean of the merger's distorting effects.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a PE in the 57-58x range, the market is pricing sustained double-digit-plus growth and margin durability well beyond what management's own '15% annual growth' guidance implies -- if that guidance is the honest forward read (and it is the most reliable anchor available given how merger-distorted the trailing reported figures are), the current multiple looks rich rather than justified by fundamentals alone, though animal-health/API businesses can carry premium multiples when genuinely scaling globally. Growth here is estimated well below the 25% hypergrowth band (deliberately discounting the base-effect-inflated trailing figures), so the ROE/dilution disclosure is not separately triggered.
escalation_reason: This stock underwent a court-approved merger (Sequent Scientific + Viyash Life Sciences, NCLT 2024) and rename (to Viyash Scientific, January 2026) very recently. The quant screen's own growth_divergence_flag is already True, its quality_score (7.9) is driven by a -3.41% trailing ROE that more current data shows as positive (about 7.4% last year), and reported YoY revenue growth varies from about 13.8% to 58.6% depending on source/period basis -- classic merger/demerger base-effect distortion of the kind the skill explicitly warns against crediting at face value. This is worth a portfolio-manager/methodology look because (a) the current quality_score likely understates this business's true current profitability, and (b) any other recently-merged or renamed name elsewhere in the 750-stock universe could carry the same distortion in the automated quant scoring, which is a systematic point beyond this one stock.
technical_commentary: Viyash Life Sciences round-tripped hard after its 2021 listing pop (Rs312 ATH down to a Rs62 low in 2023) before staging a powerful, sustained recovery since -- up roughly 4.5x off the 2023 low with a clean bullish monthly MA stack (price > 10m > 20m > 40m) and now within -11% of retaking its old 2021 high. This reads as a genuine Stage 2 breakout out of a long base, not a return to old strength on fumes.
